shared:
Repaint the attached grey block-out as ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game.

Style: that of the attached style board. Crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate or tilt the view. The foot of the lower-left wall runs parallel to the plinth's lower-left edge and the foot of the lower-right wall parallel to its lower-right edge: both walls equally steep, neither flatter than the block-out's. Do not turn the building towards the viewer: the lower-right wall is seen as much from the side as the lower-left wall. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint. The building stands on it and fills it: its outer walls rise from the plinth's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects in front of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

references.base: References: the first is the style board. The second is this building as it is in the game today: take its materials, details and character from it, but not its angle or its footprint; the block-out sets those.
references.turn: References: the first is the style board. The second is this same building in view r0, seen from the front, laid onto its footprint at exactly the block-out's camera and scale. Paint the SAME building at the same size, turned on a turntable while the camera stays where it is. It is not a mirror image: show the walls named under View, and carry the same materials, roof, colours and details round the building.
references.next: References: the first is the style board. The second is this building in the age before, laid onto its footprint at exactly the block-out's camera, scale and place: keep its footprint, its place on it and everything listed under Keep, with the new walls on the same ground lines; it may grow taller or more substantial where its age says so. Rebuild it in the materials and forms of this age. It must read as the same building, modernised.
references.sibling: References: the first is the style board. The second is the main-line depot of the same age, laid onto its own footprint: match its materials and details. This shed is smaller, with one portal in each end wall.
references.repaint: References: the first is the style board. The second is this very picture as it was painted before, laid onto its footprint and straightened to exactly the block-out's camera, scale and place. Paint the SAME building again, wall for wall and detail for detail, with its wall feet on the lines they run along in this reference. Straightening has stretched or squashed it a little: keep its wall feet exactly, and give everything above them natural proportions again.
references.mood: The last reference is a mood board for this age: take only its materials and mood from it, never its perspective, its landscape or its trains.

ages.a0: Steam age, the first railway: small and rural. Timber framing, cream limestone, warm brick, slate roofs, cast-iron posts, evergreen-painted woodwork, a chimney where it makes sense.
ages.a1: Diesel age: larger and more industrial, still of the same countryside. Warm brick walls on cream stone bases, riveted iron and steel trusses, slate or corrugated roofs with roof lights, big sliding doors, iron cranes and tanks, forest-green paint.
ages.a2: Electric age: refined and civic. Dressed cream stone, tall arched windows, glass-and-iron canopies and roof lanterns, slim dark-green steel, ceramic insulators and small gantries, tidy equipment.
ages.a3: Nuclear age: broad and substantial. Massive cream stone and smooth concrete with rounded shoulders, deep arched openings, low domes, olive-green armoured doors and panels, rows of cooling fins, small amber lamps.
ages.a4: Magnetic age: light and elegant. Smooth cream-white walls with forest-green bands, slender columns, long calm curves, ribbons of teal glass, planted green roofs, copper coil details, no visible bolts.
ages.a5: Hyper age: calm pastoral futurism. Cream tubes and rings set on cream stone bases, wide teal glass fronts under round arches, slate-dark roof blades, copper trim; no neon and no glow.

views.r0: The front faces the lower left. The lower-left wall is the FRONT; the lower-right wall is the building's right-hand side (to the right of someone standing outside and facing the front).
views.r1: The building is turned a quarter turn clockwise seen from above. The front faces the upper left, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the right-hand side; the lower-right wall is the BACK, plainer than the front.
views.r2: The building is turned half round. The front faces the upper right, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the BACK, plainer than the front; the lower-right wall is the left-hand side.
views.r3: The building is turned three quarter turns clockwise seen from above. The front faces the lower right. The lower-left wall is the left-hand side; the lower-right wall is the FRONT.

depot.what: A two-track engine shed that trains run through: one hall, as wide as it is long, with a portal for each of its two tracks in both end walls.
depot.keep: two train portals side by side in each end wall, clearly open and tall enough for a locomotive. Each portal is a doorway into the hall, and the inside of the hall shows through it: inside each doorway paint the hall's inner wall, in shadow. Only the floor is left out: below that inner wall the ground inside the doorway, up to about a third of the doorway's height, and the ground before it stay unpainted and transparent, so that the game's rails show there. Do not make the whole doorway transparent, and paint no floor, threshold, apron or rails. Also keep: one hall on a square footprint; a small crew door in the front wall
depot.front: the side wall with the crew door and windows; the tracks run through the hall parallel to it
